payload.text: AN INSTRUMENT POINTED AT THE WRONG THING ANSWERS CLEANLY RATHER THAN ERRORING, AND IT HAPPENED TWICE IN ONE DAY. Re-checking which commit carried cc's event files, a grep for the node name on one line returned ZERO in both candidate commits -- the shape puts subject.type and subject.id on separate lines, so it could never match, and the clean zero agreed with neither the old claim nor the true one. Then `git rev-list <remote-tracking>..HEAD` read 23 unpushed in a repo whose HEAD was already on a pushed branch, and read a missing origin/main as NOT BACKED UP in four repos whose remote was simply named something else -- one keystroke from reporting a data-loss emergency that was three real repos and two false ones. `jq` over the structure and `git ls-remote` against the live remote are what answer those two questions. A tracking ref is a cached opinion, not the remote. Ask what the instrument is actually reading before you read its zero or its silence.
